visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately shows the projectile on axes with a parabolic path, component vectors, and the correct flight time, whereas Lesson 2’s title visual misleadingly shows a mostly horizontal launch despite the 30° label and its mid-frame timer reads 0.00 s while displaying a nonzero time formula.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired fill-in gate after act_decomposition with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, and feedback, whereas Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning checkpoints.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, natural narration with appropriate spoken math and pacing, while Lesson 2 has no available narration transcript and therefore cannot demonstrate any audio quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 provides timed cues that generally coincide with the narration’s visual references, while Lesson 2 has no transcript or cue data available, making its synchronization absent and unevaluable.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly and clearly teaches projectile range by decomposing velocity, solving vertical flight time, and applying constant horizontal motion, whereas Lesson 2 has no available script or plan to establish mathematical correctness or pedagogical explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has larger, more legible typography, a consistent polished visual style, and no visible UI/control clutter, while Lesson 1 is cleaner than average but has cramped top text, tiny low-contrast graph labels, visible player controls, and a more utilitarian/off-balanced layout.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 1 is the clear overall winner, taking five of six dimensions with very high confidence: visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and concept accuracy. The agents consistently found Lesson 1 to have correct projectile visuals, functioning checkpoints, clear narration, aligned timing cues, and sound mathematical instruction. Lesson 2 only won polish, with good typography and cleaner presentation, but it lacked available narration, interactivity, synchronization data, and instructional/script evidence, and it had a misleading launch visual. The single polish advantage is not enough to outweigh Lesson 1’s strong wins across the core instructional dimensions.
